instructions.text: Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces and season lightly with salt.
Melt half the butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
Add the garam masala, cumin, turmeric, and chili powder. Toast the spices for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add the tomato paste and canned tomatoes. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the chicken and simmer until cooked through.
Stir in the remaining butter and the cream. Simmer gently for 2 more minutes and adjust salt to taste.
Serve hot over basmati rice.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chili powder, and toast for 30 seconds.
Add the canned tomatoes and simmer until slightly reduced.
Add the chickpeas with their liquid. Simmer until thickened, mashing a few chickpeas against the pot to thicken the sauce.
Season with salt to taste and top with fresh cilantro.
Serve hot over basmati rice.
Thaw the spinach and roughly puree it in a blender with a splash of water.
Cut the paneer into cubes. Pan-fry in a little oil until lightly golden on each side, then set aside.
In the same pan, heat the remaining oil and toast the cumin seeds until they sizzle.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then add the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the pureed spinach and garam masala. Simmer gently.
Fold in the cream and paneer, and warm through without boiling.
Season with salt and serve hot with naan.
Rinse the lentils until the water runs mostly clear.
Simmer the lentils with the turmeric in enough water to cover by an inch, until soft.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a small pan. Add the mustard and cumin seeds and cook until they pop.
Add the onion and cook until golden, then the garlic and ginger, cooking until fragrant.
Stir in the chopped tomato and cook until it breaks down.
Pour the onion-tomato mixture into the cooked lentils and stir to combine. Season with salt.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot over basmati rice.
Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear and set aside to drain.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot. Add the bay leaf and cumin seeds and cook until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook until golden, then add the garlic and ginger.
Add the carrots, garam masala, and cardamom, and stir to coat.
Add the rice and enough water to cook it through, along with the peas. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat until the rice is tender.
Let the rice rest off the heat, covered, for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
Garnish with cilantro and serve with a dollop of yogurt.
Season the chicken breasts with salt, pepper, and half the oregano.
Grill or pan-sear the chicken over medium-high heat until cooked through and lightly charred.
Rest the chicken for a few minutes, then slice.
Chop the cucumber and tomatoes into large chunks, and thinly slice the red onion.
Toss the vegetables and olives with the olive oil, lemon juice, and remaining oregano.
Top the salad with crumbled feta and the sliced chicken. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Heat the olive oil in a pot. Add the onion and cook until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, and paprika, and cook until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas with their liquid. Simmer until slightly thickened.
Stir in the spinach and cook until just wilted.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice and season with salt to taste.
Serve warm with pita bread.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Slice the zucchini and toss with a little olive oil, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan. Place the salmon fillets alongside.
Mix the minced garlic with the remaining olive oil and lemon juice, and spoon over the salmon.
Roast until the salmon flakes easily and the zucchini is tender.
Meanwhile, pour boiling water or hot broth over the couscous, cover, and let it steam.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and stir in the chopped parsley.
Serve the salmon and zucchini over the couscous with a lemon wedge.

title: Falafel-Style Chickpea Patties with Tahini Sauce

instructions.text: Pat the chickpeas dry and pulse them in a food processor with the garlic, cumin, coriander, and parsley until coarsely ground — not pureed.
Mix in the flour until the mixture holds together, then shape into small patties.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Pan-fry the patties until golden and crisp on both sides.
Whisk the tahini with lemon juice and a splash of water until smooth and pourable, seasoning with salt.
Serve the patties warm in pita with tahini sauce drizzled over top.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, and paprika, and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the canned tomatoes and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Make small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each one.
Cover and cook until the egg whites are set but the yolks are still soft.
Crumble feta over top and serve straight from the pan with pita bread.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente.
Meanwhile, cut the chicken into thin strips and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan and cook the chicken until golden and cooked through. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, cook the garlic until fragrant, then add the cream and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the parmesan until the sauce is smooth, then return the chicken to the pan.
Toss the drained pasta through the sauce and garnish with parsley and black pepper.
Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks.
Drain excess fat, then stir in the chili powder, cumin, and a splash of water. Simmer until thickened.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or in the oven.
Dice the tomato and red onion, and shred the lettuce.
Assemble the tacos with beef, cheddar, tomato, onion, lettuce, and cilantro.
Finish with a squeeze of lime and a dollop of sour cream.
Brown the ground beef in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the onion, garlic, and bell pepper, and cook until softened.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, and paprika, and toast for 30 seconds.
Add the canned tomatoes and black beans with their liquid. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Season with salt to taste and serve topped with shredded cheddar.
Preheat the oven to 210°C (410°F).
Cut the potatoes and carrots into similarly sized chunks.
Toss the chicken, potatoes, and carrots with olive oil, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan.
Roast until the chicken and potatoes are almost cooked through.
Add the broccoli florets to the pan and toss with the remaining oil.
Return to the oven and roast until the chicken is fully cooked and the vegetables are tender.
Divide the ground beef into four patties, season with salt and pepper, and press a shallow dimple in the center of each.
Cook the bacon in a pan until crisp, then set aside.
In the same pan, cook the patties over medium-high heat to your desired doneness, topping with cheddar in the last minute.
Toast the buns lightly in the same pan.
Slice the tomato and red onion.
Assemble the burgers with mustard, lettuce, tomato, onion, and bacon.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and add the cumin seeds. When they sizzle, add the onion and cook until softened.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chili and cook for 1 minute.
Add the turmeric, ground coriander and salt, then the tomatoes. Cook, stirring, until the tomatoes break down.
Add the potatoes and cauliflower, toss to coat, splash in 60 ml water, cover and cook on medium-low until tender, stirring every few minutes.
Uncover, sprinkle over the garam masala and cook a few minutes more to dry off any liquid. Finish with cilantro.
Whisk the eggs with the salt in a bowl.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add the onion and green chili and cook until the onion is soft.
Add the tomato, turmeric and chili powder and cook until the tomato softens.
Lower the heat, pour in the eggs and stir gently until just set but still soft.
Fold through the cilantro and serve with warm naan.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds, then the onion, and cook until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground chicken and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the coriander, turmeric, chili powder and salt, then the tomatoes.
Cover and simmer until the tomatoes have cooked down into the meat.
Add the peas and garam masala and cook until the peas are hot.
Scatter with cilantro and serve with basmati rice.
Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, cumin and salt until smooth, adding a spoonful or two of the reserved chickpea liquid to loosen.
Spread a thick layer of hummus over each tortilla, leaving a border.
Layer on the lettuce, cucumber, carrot and tomato.
Roll up tightly, tucking in the sides, and cut in half to serve. Leftover hummus keeps in the fridge for 4 days.
Mix the juice of half the lemon with 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 cloves of garlic (grated), the oregano, salt and pepper. Toss the chicken in it.
For the tzatziki, stir the grated cucumber, remaining garlic, remaining lemon juice and 1 tbsp olive oil into the Greek yogurt. Season with a pinch of salt.
Cook the chicken in a hot grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Warm the pitas in the pan.
Fill each pita with chicken, tomato, red onion and a generous spoonful of tzatziki.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F).

Put the tomatoes and garlic in a baking dish, set the feta block in the middle, drizzle everything with the olive oil and season with the salt, pepper and chili flakes. Bake until the tomatoes burst and the feta is soft.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain.
Mash the feta and tomatoes together in the dish, adding a splash of pasta water to make a creamy sauce.
Toss in the pasta, and the spinach if using, until coated. Finish with torn basil.

ingredients.note: thinned with lemon and water, to drizzle

instructions.text: Mix half the yogurt with the juice of half the lemon, the garlic, cumin, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, salt and olive oil. Coat the chicken thighs and let them sit while the rice cooks.
Rinse the rice and cook it with 3 cups of water, covered, over low heat.
Cook the chicken in a hot skillet over medium-high heat until charred and cooked through, turning once.
Rest the chicken, then slice it.
Build bowls with rice, chicken, lettuce, cucumber and tomato. Top with the remaining yogurt and a drizzle of tahini.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F).
Toss the sweet potato with the olive oil, chili powder, cumin and salt and roast on a sheet pan until tender and browned at the edges.
Warm the black beans in a small pot with a splash of water and a squeeze of lime.
Char the tortillas briefly in a dry pan or over a gas flame.
Fill the tortillas with sweet potato and beans, then top with avocado, red onion, cilantro, a squeeze of lime and sour cream if you like.

ingredients.note: melted, plus more for the pan

instructions.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the milk, eggs and melted butter.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir until just combined — a few lumps are fine.
Heat a lightly buttered pan over medium heat. Pour in about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake and cook until bubbles appear on top.
Flip and cook until golden underneath.
Keep warm while you cook the rest. Serve with honey.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper.
Melt half the butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the bell pepper until softened, then add the spinach and green onion and cook until wilted. Set the vegetables aside.
Melt the rest of the butter, pour in half the eggs and cook, pulling the set edges into the middle, until almost set.
Spoon half the vegetables and cheese over one side, fold, and slide onto a plate.
Repeat with the remaining eggs and filling for a second omelette. Cut each in half to serve four.
Rinse the rice and cook it with 3 cups of water, covered, over low heat.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat and stir-fry the chicken until cooked through. Remove.
Add the remaining oil, then the broccoli, carrot and bell pepper. Stir-fry until crisp-tender, adding a splash of water if the pan is dry.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then return the chicken, pour in the sauce and toss until glossy.
Serve over rice, scattered with green onion.
Rinse the rice and cook it with 3 cups of water, covered, over low heat.
Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu, turning, until golden and crisp on most sides. Remove.
Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar and sesame oil together.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the broccoli, bell pepper and carrot until crisp-tender.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, return the tofu, pour over the sauce and toss to coat.
Serve over rice with green onion.
Cook the pasta in boiling water until just tender. Reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking water, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic and ginger, loosening with the reserved water until pourable.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, cucumber, carrot and most of the green onion.
Top with the remaining green onion and chili flakes. Good cold the next day for lunch.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and celery until softened.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in the broth and add the bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer, add the whole chicken breasts and poach gently until cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and discard the bay leaves.
Add the pasta to the pot and simmer until tender.
Return the chicken, season with salt and pepper, and stir in the parsley.

ingredients.note: cooked and cooled — day-old is best

instructions.text: If you don't have leftover rice, cook it with 3 cups of water, then spread it on a tray to cool and dry before frying.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat. Cook the shrimp until pink, then remove.
Scramble the eggs in the wok until just set, then remove.
Add the remaining oil, the carrot, peas and corn, and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the garlic.
Add the rice and fry, pressing it against the hot wok, until heated through and slightly crisp.
Return the shrimp and egg, add the soy sauce, sesame oil and most of the green onion, and toss. Top with the rest of the green onion.
